s: LI-RAGE achieves the best reported performance on NQ-TABLES and E2E-WTQ, with gains attributed largely to the LI retriever. s: It presents a syntax-aware retrieval augmented method for code generation and addresses noise and search-cost challenges in retrieval-based generation.

l: neural code generation, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation / Abstract
s: It automatically generates code from natural-language descriptions and is widely adopted.

s: It can suffer from extraneous retrieval noise that results in syntactically incorrect code, while frequent cached-datastore searches can be time-consuming.

l: kNN-TRANX, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation / Abstract
s: It is a token-level retrieval augmented code generation method that searches smaller datastores tailored for code generation. It uses syntax constraints for datastore retrieval, and experiments on two public datasets confirm its effectiveness.

l: token-level retrieval, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation / Abstract
s: It has shown potential in neural machine translation, but applying it directly to code generation introduces retrieval noise and search overhead.

l: datastore, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation / Abstract
s: It is searched to support retrieval-based generation, and kNN-TRANX uses smaller datastores tailored to code generation. Syntax constraints are used to guide datastore retrieval and reduce the impact of retrieval noise.

l: Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 1
s: This unit concerns neural code generation and the proposed kNN-TRANX approach for mapping natural-language descriptions to code. It explains that directly applying kNN-MT introduces retrieval noise, syntactic errors, and costly datastore searches. kNN-TRANX instead generates abstract syntax trees using separate syntactic and semantic datastores, grammar-based filtering, and a combination of neural and kNN probabilities. On CoNaLa and Django, kNN-TRANX improves exact match or BLEU over compared models, and its datastore-switching adaptation reduces trainable parameters by 7,000 times while achieving performance comparable to fully fine-tuned models.

l: neural code generation, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 1
s: Neural code generation maps natural-language input to code snippets using deep learning. The unit describes kNN-TRANX as an approach intended to improve its performance, syntactic correctness, and deployment efficiency.

l: neural machine translation, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 1
s: Neural machine translation has recently advanced the non-parametric k-nearest-neighbour machine translation approach, which can improve standard neural machine translation models by adding token-level retrieval.

l: kNN-MT, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 1
s: kNN-MT equips generation models with a token-level retriever and can improve their performance. When applied directly to code generation, it may retrieve noisy tokens, produce syntactically invalid code, and require a similarity search over the entire datastore at every inference step.

l: token-level retrieval, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 1
s: The token-level retriever integrates external knowledge into a pretrained model and allows the model to be updated by switching the retrieval datastore without fine-tuning model parameters. Its use in kNN-MT can introduce irrelevant retrieved tokens into generated code.

l: neural-retrieval-in-the-loop approach, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 1
s: The neural-retrieval-in-the-loop approach integrates retrieval into generation to add external knowledge and support datastore-based updates. For code generation, the unit reports that it suffers from retrieval noise, lacks guaranteed syntactic correctness, and has expensive token-level searches.

l: kNN-TRANX, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 1
s: The code generation approach kNN-TRANX generates abstract syntax trees instead of code snippets directly. It uses grammar rules, separate datastores, retrieval filtering, and a learnable confidence parameter to combine kNN and neural probabilities, improving results on CoNaLa and Django.

l: seq2tree model, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 1
s: The sequence-to-tree model is used by kNN-TRANX to generate an abstract syntax tree rather than a target code snippet directly. This enables AST construction rules to enforce syntactic correctness and filter retrieval noise.

l: AST, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 1
s: The abstract syntax tree is a hierarchical tree-like structure representing code. kNN-TRANX generates it through AST construction actions so that grammar rules can constrain the resulting code.

l: AST construction rules, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 1
s: AST construction rules are used to guarantee the syntactic correctness of generated code and filter out retrieval noise. They determine the type of the next node and help eliminate irrelevant retrieval results.

l: syntactic datastore, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 1
s: The syntactic datastore is one of two separate datastores constructed by kNN-TRANX according to AST node type. It is queried when the grammar indicates that a syntactic node should be predicted.

l: semantic datastore, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 1
s: The semantic datastore is constructed separately from the syntactic datastore based on AST node type. kNN-TRANX queries the appropriate datastore after determining the next node type from grammar rules.

l: model canonical incremental adaptation, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 1
s: Model canonical incremental adaptation is evaluated by updating kNN-TRANX through datastore switching. The unit reports that this achieves performance comparable to fully fine-tuned models while reducing trainable parameters by 7,000 times.

l: CoNaLa dataset, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 1
s: CoNaLa is one of the publicly available code generation datasets used to evaluate kNN-TRANX. The approach achieves a 27.6% improvement in exact match on this dataset.

l: Django dataset, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 1
s: Django is one of the publicly available code generation datasets used to evaluate kNN-TRANX. The approach achieves a 4.2% improvement in BLEU on this dataset.

l: Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.2
s: This unit introduces the kNN-MT paradigm and seq2tree models. kNN-MT enhances NMT model generation by retrieving knowledge from a datastore of decoder hidden states paired with target tokens. Seq2tree models generate abstract syntax trees (ASTs) rather than code snippets, helping ensure syntactic correctness. BertranX is presented as a state-of-the-art seq2tree architecture that uses BERT, a grammar-based decoder, and ASDL-based action sequences.

l: kNN-MT, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.2
s: kNN-MT is a translation mechanism that enhances model generation by incorporating an additional translation retriever. During inference, it retrieves datastore entries using the contextual representation and combines the retrieved target-token probabilities according to distance and temperature.

l: NMT model, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.2
s: The NMT model generates decoder context representations from a source sentence and preceding target tokens. These representations are used as keys when building the datastore.

l: datastore, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.2
s: The datastore is built from key-value pairs in which each key is a decoder hidden state and each value is its corresponding target token. During inference, kNN-MT retrieves entries from the datastore to support token generation.

l: seq2tree model, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.2
s: Seq2tree models generate ASTs instead of directly outputting code snippets. Compared with seq2seq models, they ensure the syntactic correctness of generated code.

l: AST, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.2
s: ASTs are generated by seq2tree models rather than direct code snippets. BertranX describes ASTs using sequences of actions based on ASDL grammar.

l: BertranX, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.2
s: BertranX is described as a state-of-the-art seq2tree architecture. It uses BERT to process input natural language, a grammar-based decoder, and ASDL-based action sequences to generate ASTs.

l: ASDL grammar, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.2
s: ASDL provides concise notations for describing the abstract syntax of programming languages. In BertranX, it defines grammatical symbols and supports action sequences for describing ASTs.

l: PREDRULE, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.2
s: PREDRULE is an action type used to initiate the generation of a new node from its parent node. It is marked as a syntactic node.

l: GENERATE, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 2 / 2.1 .. 2.2
s: GENERATE is an action type used to produce terminal or primitive symbols. It is marked as a semantic node.

l: Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.2
s: kNN-TRANX is a seq2tree-based approach with separate datastore building and model inferring components. During datastore building, it parses the training dataset's code snippets into abstract syntax trees and stores decoder representations with target rules or primitives in separate syntactic and semantic datastores. During inference, kNN-TRANX generates a context representation and neural network distribution, retrieves a k-nearest-neighbor distribution using syntax constraints and ASDL grammar, and combines the distributions. The meta-k network dynamically weights different retrieval sizes, while the confidence network estimates how to weight the kNN and neural network distributions.

l: kNN-TRANX, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.2
s: kNN-TRANX consists of datastore building and model inferring components. It uses separate syntactic and semantic datastores, syntax-constrained retrieval, a meta-k network, and a confidence network to combine retrieved and neural predictions.

l: seq2tree model, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.2
s: The seq2tree model is pre-trained and used with the training dataset to generate decoder context representations. During inference, it produces the context representation and neural network distribution for the current code fragment.

l: training dataset, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.2
s: The training dataset is paired with a pre-trained seq2tree model to construct the datastores. Its code snippets are parsed into abstract syntax trees, and the resulting context representations and target tokens are stored as key-value pairs.

l: AST, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.2
s: The abstract syntax tree represents each code snippet and consists of actions categorized as rules and primitives. Structural nodes are associated with rules, while semantic nodes are associated with primitives.

l: syntactic datastore, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.2
s: The syntactic datastore stores context representations as keys and target rules as values. It is retrieved when the subsequent token is expected to represent syntactic information.

l: semantic datastore, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.2
s: The semantic datastore stores context representations as keys and target primitives as values. It is retrieved when the subsequent token is expected to represent semantic information.

l: probability from the neural network, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.2
s: The neural network distribution is computed from the current context representation by the trained model. It is combined with the k-nearest-neighbor distribution using a confidence value.

l: k-nearest-neighbor distribution, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.2
s: The k-nearest-neighbor distribution is obtained by querying a datastore with the current context representation and mapping neighbor distances to probabilities. kNN-TRANX combines distributions from multiple retrieval sizes using weights produced by the meta-k network.

l: syntax-constrained token-level retrieval, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.2
s: Syntax-constrained token-level retrieval selects neighbors according to the expected type of the subsequent token. It uses the generated tokens and ASDL grammar to choose the relevant datastore and exclude illegitimate tokens while retaining potentially valuable knowledge.

l: ASDL grammar, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.2
s: The ASDL grammar determines which child nodes are legitimate after the tokens already produced. It is used during retrieval to filter out nodes that are not supported by the grammar.

l: meta-k network, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.2
s: The meta-k network dynamically evaluates retrieval sizes smaller than an upper bound K. It uses neighbor distances and counts of distinct values among the top neighbors to produce normalized weights for combining k-nearest-neighbor predictions.

l: Confidence Network, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.2
s: The confidence network estimates the confidence of the k-nearest-neighbor and neural network distributions. It uses both distributions and the meta-k weights to calculate a sigmoid-based confidence value for their weighted combination.

l: kNN-TRANX inference, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.2
s: kNN-TRANX inference has three phases: generating a context representation and neural network distribution, querying a datastore for a k-nearest-neighbor distribution, and combining the two distributions to predict the target token.

l: datastore building, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 3 / 3.1 .. 3.2
s: Datastore building parses training code snippets into abstract syntax trees and generates instances from the training corpus. It stores context representations as keys and separates rule values from primitive values into syntactic and semantic datastores.

l: Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.3
s: This unit reports experiments evaluating kNN-TRANX on the CoNaLa and Django code-generation datasets using BLEU, CodeBLEU, and exact match. It describes kNN-TRANX’s implementation with BertranX, separate syntactic and semantic datastores, and retrieval settings, and compares it with several code-generation models. kNN-TRANX outperforms BertranX and other listed systems, with especially clear gains on the challenging CoNaLa dataset. The unit also analyzes retrieval filtering, datastore composition and size, and model canonical incremental adaptation through datastore-only updates to avoid parameter adaptation.

l: Experiments, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.3
s: The experiments evaluate code generation and model canonical incremental adaptation. They use the CoNaLa and Django datasets and assess results with BLEU, CodeBLEU, and exact match.

l: code generation, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.3
s: The code-generation experiments compare kNN-TRANX with TRANX, Reranker, Ext-codegen, TAE, BertranX, REDCODER, and CodeT5. Token-level retrieval improves code-generation performance, with more evident gains on challenging tasks.

l: model canonical incremental adaptation, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.3
s: Model canonical incremental adaptation is evaluated by updating only the datastore rather than adapting model parameters. This setup is intended to reduce the computational cost of incremental learning and avoid catastrophic forgetting.

l: kNN-TRANX, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.3
s: kNN-TRANX uses BertranX as its base seq2tree model and creates separate syntactic and semantic datastores. It achieves 37.29 BLEU, 39.04 CodeBLEU, and 7.4 exact match on CoNaLa, and 83.20 BLEU, 81.66 CodeBLEU, and 82.16 exact match on Django, outperforming BertranX on all reported measures.

l: CoNaLa dataset, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.3
s: The CoNaLa dataset contains 600,000 NL-code pairs collected from StackOverflow, including 2,879 NL queries rewritten by developers. It covers questions programmers encounter in real-world projects and is used to evaluate kNN-TRANX.

l: Django dataset, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.3
s: The Django dataset contains 18,805 examples pairing one line of Python code with corresponding comments. Approximately 70% of its examples are simple tasks such as variable assignment, method definition, and exception handling.

l: BLEU, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.3
s: BLEU is one of the metrics used to evaluate the generated code. kNN-TRANX improves over BertranX by 3.11 BLEU on CoNaLa and 3.34 BLEU on Django.

l: CodeBLEU, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.3
s: CodeBLEU is used alongside BLEU and exact match to assess code-generation quality. kNN-TRANX improves over BertranX by 2.95 CodeBLEU on CoNaLa and 2.81 CodeBLEU on Django.

l: BertranX, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.3
s: BertranX is a BERT-encoder model used as the base model for kNN-TRANX and is trained on annotated data and 100,000 mined data. Its scores are lower than those of kNN-TRANX on both CoNaLa and Django.

l: syntactic datastore, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.3
s: The syntactic datastore stores syntactic information separately from the semantic datastore because the two datastores have substantially different vocabulary sizes. Its upper retrieval limit is set to Krule = 4, and a small amount of stored syntactic knowledge can already support high-quality code generation.

l: semantic datastore, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.3
s: The semantic datastore is configured with Kpri = 64 and stores semantic information separately from syntactic information. Generated-code quality continues to improve as the semantic datastore grows, which the text attributes to the relative scarcity of semantic knowledge.

l: datastore, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.3
s: kNN-TRANX creates two datastores and uses FAISS for similarity retrieval. Increasing datastore size improves generated-code quality, while placing syntactic and semantic actions in the same datastore substantially reduces quality by introducing noise.

l: retrieval filtering, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.3
s: The ablation study finds that retrieval filtering significantly improves code-generation performance. The approach that jointly considers the neural-network and kNN distributions performs better than the compared adaptive kNN-box distance method.

l: incremental learning, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 4 / 4.1 .. 4.3
s: Incremental learning is described as necessary for continuously updating trained code-generation models, but it consumes substantial computing resources. Using new data for incremental learning can also cause catastrophic forgetting, motivating datastore-only updates in the adaptation evaluation.

l: Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, opening
s: This unit evaluates BertranX and kNN-TRANX on the CoNaLa dataset and Django dataset, including ablations of noise filtering, the Confidence Network, and separate datastores. It studies how different Krule and Kpri values affect CoNaLa results, with kNN-TRANX reaching 37.29 BLEU, 39.04 CodeBLEU, and 7.4 EM at Krule=4 and Kpri=64. In an incremental learning scenario, the datastore is updated with 0k, 10k, 50k, or 95k mined data, requiring 17k trainable parameters instead of 122,205k for fine-tuning all parameters. l: CoNaLa dataset, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, opening
s: The CoNaLa dataset is used to evaluate BertranX and kNN-TRANX, conduct ablation studies, and study different Krule and Kpri settings. Its mined data contains substantial irrelevant content that adds noise to retrieval.

l: Django dataset, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, opening
s: The Django dataset is used alongside the CoNaLa dataset to evaluate the ablation variants. kNN-TRANX achieves 83.20 BLEU, 81.66 CodeBLEU, and 82.16 EM on Django.

l: BertranX, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, opening
s: BertranX is evaluated as a baseline on the CoNaLa and Django datasets, achieving 34.18 BLEU, 36.09 CodeBLEU, and 5.8 EM on CoNaLa, and 79.86 BLEU, 78.85 CodeBLEU, and 79.77 EM on Django.

l: kNN-TRANX, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, opening
s: kNN-TRANX outperforms BertranX in the reported CoNaLa and Django results and improves as datastore knowledge is updated. Without additional datastore data, kNN-TRANX† can also outperform BertranX†, while 95k external data yields BLEU comparable to training-based BertranX.

l: incremental learning, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, opening
s: Incremental learning is examined by updating the datastore with 0k, 10k, 50k, or 95k mined data from the CoNaLa dataset. The updates improve kNN-TRANX on all three evaluation criteria.

l: datastore, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, opening
s: The model uses separate datastores for syntactic and semantic information. Updating the datastore enables efficient fine-tuning with 17k trainable parameters rather than training all 122,205k parameters.

s: The syntactic datastore contains 109 token types and 1,603k entries. The text reports that even a small amount of syntactic knowledge can improve model performance.

s: The semantic datastore contains 518k entries in the reported experiment, with vocabulary-dependent token types and relatively scarce knowledge per vocabulary. Updating only the semantic datastore can still improve performance.

s: Fine-tuning all parameters would require training 122,205k parameters, whereas the described datastore-update method trains only 17k parameters. The method therefore greatly reduces GPU memory consumption while achieving comparable results.

s: Mined data from the CoNaLa dataset is used in updates of 0k, 10k, 50k, and 95k. Much of the mined data is irrelevant to the NL-code pairs, adding noise to retrieval.

l: Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 5
s: This unit reviews code generation and retrieval-augmented models. Yin and Neubig (2018) propose TRANX for generating ASTs, while later work introduces grammar-based decoding, reliability improvements, and test-case-based code selection. It also describes pre-training as a way to incorporate external knowledge and improve downstream performance. Retrieval-based methods include REDCODER, kNN-MT, and Fast kNN-MT, and Figure 5 examines how reducing datastore size affects BLEU and CodeBLEU on the CoNaLa and Django datasets.

l: code generation, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 5
s: Code generation aims to produce target code from natural language to improve programmers' development efficiency. The unit discusses AST-based generation, reliability improvements, test-case-based selection, and the benefits of large-scale pre-training models.

l: TRANX, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 5
s: Yin and Neubig (2018) propose TRANX, which generates abstract syntax trees instead of directly generating code snippets.

l: pre-training, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 5
s: Pre-training methods are used to incorporate more external knowledge into models and improve performance on downstream tasks. Large-scale pre-training models have recently shown strong capabilities in code generation.

l: Retrieval-augmented models, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 5
s: Retrieval-augmented models retrieve and integrate auxiliary sentences or other information to improve generation. The unit describes their use in adapting to inputs, generating code through searched action subtrees, and improving code generation and translation.

l: REDCODER, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 5
s: Parvez et al. (2021) propose REDCODER, which uses retrieved natural-language code to improve code generation and code translation models.

l: kNN-MT, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 5
s: Khandelwal et al. (2021) propose kNN-MT, which constructs a datastore using decoder representations as keys and corresponding target characters as values. Generation retrieves the top k neighbors, and later work improves the paradigm's retrieval weighting and robustness.

l: Fast kNN-MT, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 5
s: Meng et al. (2022) propose Fast kNN-MT, which improves retrieval efficiency by constructing multiple smaller datastores.

l: CoNaLa dataset, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 5
s: The CoNaLa dataset is used in Figure 5 to examine how datastore size affects BLEU and CodeBLEU. The figure evaluates reductions in syntactic knowledge, semantic knowledge, and both types of knowledge.

l: Django dataset, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 5
s: The Django dataset is used in Figure 5 to examine how datastore size affects BLEU and CodeBLEU. The figure evaluates reductions in syntactic knowledge, semantic knowledge, and both types of knowledge.

l: datastore, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 5
s: A datastore in kNN-MT stores decoder representations as keys and corresponding target characters as values for retrieval. Figure 5 studies the effect of reducing datastore size by removing syntactic knowledge, semantic knowledge, or both.

l: Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 6
s: The paper proposes kNN-TRANX, a seq2tree model supported by syntactic and semantic datastores. It reports that kNN-TRANX outperforms the baselines and can switch datastores to provide additional knowledge without fine-tuning the neural network. Experiments show competitive performance against learning-based methods through incremental learning. Table 5 evaluates model canonical incremental adaptation by updating both datastores or only the semantic datastore with external data.

l: kNN-TRANX, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 6
s: kNN-TRANX provides syntactic and semantic datastores for a seq2tree model and outperforms the baselines. It can switch datastores without fine-tuning the neural network and achieves competitive performance through incremental learning. s: BertranX serves as the underlying model for kNN-TRANX and as a baseline in the experiments. BertranX†, trained on cleaned 2k and mined 5k data, obtains 29.22 BLEU, 29.89 CodeBLEU, and 4.0 EM, while the full BertranX obtains 34.18 BLEU, 36.09 CodeBLEU, and 5.8 EM.

s: The syntactic datastore is one of the datastores provided for the kNN-TRANX seq2tree model. In canonical incremental adaptation, it is updated simultaneously with the semantic datastore when Only Semantics is false, but is not the datastore updated when Only Semantics is true.

l: semantic datastore, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 6
s: The semantic datastore is one of the datastores provided for the kNN-TRANX seq2tree model. It can be updated without fine-tuning the neural network, and when Only Semantics is true, it is the only datastore updated with external data.

l: incremental learning, Syntax-Aware Retrieval Augmented Code Generation, 6
s: Incremental learning enables kNN-TRANX to achieve competitive performance against learning-based methods. The experiments use external data to incrementally update the datastores without fine-tuning the neural network.

s: Model canonical incremental adaptation is evaluated in Table 5 by updating the datastores with 10k, 50k, or 95k external data. Updating more external data generally improves kNN-TRANX's BLEU, CodeBLEU, and EM results, whether both datastores or only the semantic datastore is updated.
